name: Swag Labs (SauceDemo)
facts: Swag Labs is a small e-commerce demo store used for UI automation practice. Flow: log in, browse a 6-item product inventory, sort it, add items to the cart, then a three-step checkout (address form, order overview, confirmation). A hamburger menu holds Logout and Reset App State. Several accounts exist to exercise failure paths: locked_out_user cannot log in, problem_user renders broken images and misbehaving controls, performance_glitch_user responds slowly, error_user and visual_user break specific interactions. Application state (cart contents) is stored per browser session and can be reset from the menu. The product sort control (data-test="product-sort-container") takes the option values az, za, lohi and hilo, and the applied option's label is shown in data-test="active-option". Add-to-cart controls are REPLACED rather than relabelled: after clicking data-test="add-to-cart-<slug>" that element is gone and a separate data-test="remove-<slug>" element takes its place. A test that expects the add button to change its text fails with 'element(s) not found'. The same applies on the product detail page.

pages.name: login
pages.note: Entry page. The accepted usernames and the shared password are printed on the page itself.

pages.name: login_error
pages.note: Rejected login. No path on purpose: navigating would wipe the error banner. locked_out_user is one of the deliberately broken accounts.

pages.name: inventory
pages.note: Product list with sort dropdown and per-item add-to-cart buttons.

pages.name: item_detail
pages.note: Single product view reached by clicking a product title. Has its own add-to-cart control, which is REPLACED by a remove control once clicked, and a 'Back to products' link.

pages.name: item_detail_added
pages.note: The detail page AFTER adding, where the add control has been replaced by data-test="remove". Captured as its own page because that replacement selector is otherwise never observed, and a planner may only use observed selectors - so without this the only assertion it can express is that add-to-cart changes its text, which is not what the application does. The note on item_detail already said so in prose; prose does not constrain a planner that copies selectors from a list. Readiness is the remove control itself, which is true only in the state being captured.

pages.name: cart
pages.note: Captured with one item already added, so the populated state is visible.

pages.name: checkout_step_one
pages.note: Address form: first name, last name, postal code.

pages.name: checkout_step_two
pages.note: Order overview with item total, tax and total. Finish completes the order.

pages.name: cart_two_items
pages.note: Cart holding two items, so each item's own remove control is an observed selector. Removing an item removes its row; the badge counts remaining items and disappears entirely at zero.

pages.name: inventory_sorted
pages.note: Product list sorted by price, high to low. The sort control's option values are az / za / lohi / hilo, and the currently applied one is echoed in data-test="active-option".
